pop_stats.citation: Historical population statistics of Europe (central statistical offices and demographic histories; figures for January 1914); web search was disabled, so no page-level URL/page was given; figures are from established historical statistics (± several percent uncertainty).

industry_stats.citation: Historical statistical compilations of the early 20th century (central statistical offices of Germany, France, UK, Austria-Hungary, Italy, Russia, etc.; industrial output statistics and firm statistics); no page-level URLs available because web search was disabled; based on established historical knowledge.

coal_stats.citation: Mineral production statistics of 1913 (coal commissions and industry reports of major producers: Ruhr/Saar, French industry, Walloon basin, Hungarian industry, Donbass, Kuzbass, Lorraine, etc.); compiled from historical industry reports; no page-level citations possible.

iron_stats.citation: Iron ore and pig iron output of 1913-1914 (steel and iron industry reports: Ruhr, Lorraine/Saar, Czech Moravian ore, Donbass, Sweden Kiruna, Switzerland, etc.); historical compilations; no page-level URLs because web search was disabled; figures from established historical knowledge with noted uncertainty.

oil_stats.citation: Oil production/import figures of 1913-1914 (Anglo-Persian Oil Company and trade balance sheets; Ploiesti refineries; Baku; minor Anatolian fields; net importer positions); trade statistics compiled from government trade departments; no page-level URLs available.

urban_stats.citation: Historical studies of urbanization and agglomeration for 1900-1914 (demographic histories); urban share estimates without page-level data; web search was disabled, so figures come from general historical demographic knowledge.

german_empire.coal: Ruhr district, ~150 Mt/yr (~165 Mt total incl. lignite) in 1913-1914; 1,000+ collieries
german_empire.oil: Import-driven; Upper Silesia minor fields; net importer of crude
german_empire.industry: Strong industrial base (steel, coal, chemicals, automobiles); Level A

austria_hungary.coal: Austrian and Hungarian brown coal, ~35-40 Mt/yr (Puszta fields)
austria_hungary.industry: Strong in Austria/Czechia, moderate in Hungary; modern, recently industrialising; Level A

italy.iron: Sulfur-rich ore, ~3 Mt/yr (lega MorLock legend? refined later) — approximately 3 Mt/yr
italy.industry: Growing industrial base (machinery, chemicals, arms); Level B

serbia.industry: Nascent agrarian; light local industry; Level C

bulgaria.industry: Nascent; agrarian with light industry; Level C

romania.oil: Ploiesti refineries, ~2.5 Mt/yr (major net exporter to Russia/Greece/Germany)
romania.industry: Major oil and coal producer; strong refining; Level B

greece.industry: Nascent agrarian; light industry; Level C

sweden.industry: Shipbuilding, machine tools, agriculture machinery; Level B

switzerland.industry: Chemicals, watches, precision industry; Level A

spain.industry: Agricultural base; light industry; Level C

belgium.oil: Import; slight domestic; ~1.5 Mt/yr via Antwerp (Anglo-Persian)
belgium.industry: Highly industrialized (metallurgy, chemicals, arms); Level A

united_kingdom.oil: North Sea fields starting; ~0.03 Mt/yr (public); net importer

ottoman_empire.industry: Nascent modern industry (textiles, mining); Level C

russia.coal: Donbass ~22 Mt/yr; Kuzbass ~1-2 Mt/yr + minors; total ~45 Mt/yr
russia.oil: Baku ~2.8 Mt/yr (1913 peak); smaller fields (Ekibastuz etc.)
russia.industry: Heavy industry growing (steel, rail, chemicals); Level B

luxembourg.industry: Steel, chemicals, watch parts; Level B

monaco.industry: None; Level D (tiny state; tourism/gambling economic)

key_regions.name: Ruhr
key_regions.note: Germany's principal coal basin; ~150-165 Mt/yr in 1913-1914 (1,000+ collieries); core of steel and chemicals production.

key_regions.name: Donbass
key_regions.note: Largest coal producer of the Russian Empire; ~22-30 Mt/yr in 1913 (Donets basin; production still growing, peak reached ~1917).

key_regions.name: Kuzbass
key_regions.note: Siberian coal region emerging by 1914; production growing to ~1-2 Mt/yr; Russian attempt to diversify beyond the European basins.

key_regions.name: Lorraine/Saar
key_regions.note: Major French iron basin (Haut-Moselle); ~2.5-2.8 Mt/yr; Saar shares partly German (declining as French pre-1871 ore becomes exhausted).

key_regions.name: Upper Silesia
key_regions.note: Hematite ore, high sulfur; ~1.5-2 Mt/yr; smelting centres in Silesia.

key_regions.name: Baku
key_regions.note: World's largest oil field (~2.5-2.8 Mt/yr in 1913); on the cusp of its golden age; still slightly growing.

key_regions.name: Ploiești
key_regions.note: Romania's main oil centre; ~2-3 Mt/yr of refineries; major net exporter of refined products to Russia, Greece and Germany.

uncertainties: Germany population: 65 M is the conventional figure for Jan 1914; census-era revisions and resident vs. registered differences put the true figure within ~±0.5 M. Marked moyenne.
Germany urban_share 0.5: only regional census ranges (~50-55% for 1900-1910) are documented; no source-level detail available since web search was disabled; marked moyenne.
Austria-Hungary population ~51 M: statistical compilations vary (50-53 M depending on source and statistical office); marked moyenne.
Russia oil: net importer with modest Baku exports; import/production split not precisely documented for Jan 1914; marked faible.
UK oil: North Sea fields only just beginning to produce (~20-30 kt/yr by 1914 public estimates; some sources report less); marked faible.
Italy iron output: sulfur-rich smelting figures vary by mine (2.5-3.5 Mt/yr across sources); marked moyenne.
Romania industry level B: strong oil export capacity and large coal, but industrial breadth below Germany's; rating is judgmental, marked moyenne.
Micro-states (Monaco, Andorra, Luxembourg): populations are rounded and may be off by ±30%; industry levels are placeholders with no source detail.
No page-level URLs or exact citation numbers could be produced because web search was disabled; all citations are named historical-statistics sources with reliability labels per the task.
Rounding: most resource figures are approximations in round Mt/yr units; exact production figures can differ by ±15-20% depending on source (coking plants, open-pit vs underground, lignite handling).
